Maskin Monotonicity

Two agents, three alternatives X={a,b,c}X = \{a, b, c\}X={a,b,c}. If a rule fff picks xxx at θ\thetaθ and xxx falls for no one at θ′\theta'θ′, then f(θ′)f(\theta')f(θ′) must still be xxx — a necessary condition for Nash implementation. The dictatorial rule passes; the bottom-choice rule earns a red violation.

Since xxx topped agent 1's ranking at θ\thetaθ, this means x≻1′yx \succ_1' yx≻1′​y for every y≠xy \neq xy=x — xxx is still agent 1's top choice at θ′\theta'θ′.

Since the conclusion follows for every (θ,θ′)(\theta, \theta')(θ,θ′) pair satisfying the hypothesis, the dictatorial rule is Maskin monotonic. The intuition: "if xxx was never overtaken, xxx is still first."
